solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Really impressed by Gone With the Wind

definitions.meaning: someone overwhelmed with admiration is said to be knocked out by it
literally carried off by a gust of air

explanation.surface: A viewer's verdict on the famous film: utterly bowled over by it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being amazed is also a literal phrase for being swept off by a gale, which the film title neatly echoes.

clue.text: County money, commonly

definitions.meaning: Buckinghamshire, an English county near London
dollars are informally called ... in everyday slang

explanation.surface: A query about what a shire's cash is called in everyday speech.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the standard abbreviation of the county Buckinghamshire; the other is slang for dollars.

clue.text: They're said to attract rich and poor, for instance

definitions.meaning: the proverb holds that contrasting people are drawn to each other
a pair of words contrary in meaning, as antonyms

explanation.surface: A musing that the wealthy and the needy are drawn together, like the old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb about attraction concerns contrasting things, and rich and poor are a classic antonym pair.

clue.text: It transmits messages, never brief, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone awry, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint about some messenger who is regrettably never short-winded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the ten letters of 'never brief'.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand of the nervous system carries signals as electrical impulses, so it conveys messages around the body.

clue.text: Spring collection probably wouldn't suit such figures

definitions.text: Spring collection probably wouldn't suit such figures

parts.note: a spring is a source of water, as a well is
a set is a collection of things belonging together

explanation.surface: Fashion advice: a flimsy spring range of clothes won't flatter stocky builds.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also hints at the meaning: light spring fashions tend not to flatter sturdily built people.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sturdily or strongly built describes a figure that delicate seasonal fashions would probably not flatter.

clue.text: Very wide, like Lowry's last colourful canvas

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of the painter's name

parts.note: an awning is a canvas sheet stretched over a shopfront, often brightly striped

explanation.surface: An art critic describing a broad final painting by Lowry.
explanation.walkthrough: L. S. Lowry was an English painter of northern industrial scenes; 'canvas' looks like a painting but is the shop cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaping chasm or gap is wide open, like a mouth stretched in a yawn.

clue.text: Wise guy, ignoring Washington, achieves some eminence

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out the abbreviation for the US state

parts.note: a know-all is a person who thinks they know everything
WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

explanation.surface: A smart alec who snubs Washington still rises to some prominence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eminence' looks like status, but here it is a rise in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminence is a piece of rising ground, and a small rounded hill is just that.

clue.text: Weep and wail, signifying 26

definitions.meaning: to lament loudly for the dead, as at an Irish funeral
26 across is EAGER, and ... means enthusiastic

explanation.surface: A crossref clue linking mourning cries to another answer.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the Irish funeral lament; the other is an adjective for being enthusiastic.

clue.text: Start where films are made

definitions.meaning: the beginning of something, as of an illness
the film studio stage where scenes are shot

explanation.surface: A note on where a film begins: in the studio.
explanation.definitionFit: The beginning of something is one sense; read as two words it is the film studio location.

clue.text: Former contributor to the big smoke

definitions.text: Former contributor to the big smoke

parts.words: Former contributor to the big smoke
parts.note: the Big Smoke is a nickname for London, and its old pea-souper smogs added to the haze

explanation.surface: Something that once added to a vast cloud of smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the big smoke' is British slang for London; its notorious smogs ended after the 1950s clean-air laws.
explanation.definitionFit: The thick smog of the capital literally formed the haze behind the city's smoky nickname.

clue.text: Bound carbon copy needs cover, finally

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
to ape is to imitate or copy

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word cover

explanation.surface: An office scene: a bound carbon copy that needs a cover put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like tied up, but it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to skip or leap about playfully, so it means to bound.

clue.text: Seaside in Winter, for example, from the Blue Period

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling low
a season is a period of time

explanation.surface: An artwork title, a seaside winter scene from Picasso's Blue Period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue Period' points at Picasso, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Resorts in winter see few visitors, the quiet off-peak time of year for tourism.

clue.text: She may well have her twins at sea!

definitions.text: She may well have her twins at sea!

parts.words: She may well have her twins at sea!
parts.note: ships are called she, and a vessel built to the same design as another is its twin

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman giving birth to twins aboard a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel built to the same design as another is its sibling, and vessels are traditionally feminine.

clue.text: A few guiding words (not a thousand) in German

indicators.note: not tells us to drop the Roman numeral for a thousand

parts.note: a motto is a short phrase to live by
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A short maxim, minus a thousand, written in the German language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in German' looks like the language, but the definition is a German man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A common forename among German men, as with the statesman Bismarck.

clue.text: Botanical site showing various dangers on line, say

indicators.note: on means the reshuffled dangers are placed after the soundalike of line
say signals that we use a word that sounds like a waiting line

parts.note: a queue is a line of people waiting

indicators.note: various suggests a mixed set, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A botanical site with many hazards lining up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges 'dangers'. The royal botanical gardens are in Kew, west London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London are a world-famous plant collection.

clue.text: Loyalist Irishman joins the fray

parts.note: Pat is a stock name for an Irishman, short for Patrick
a fray is a fight or disturbance, a riot

explanation.surface: A loyal Irishman wades into a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to their country is loyal to it, a supporter of the nation.

clue.text: What nudists do in long business suit

indicators.note: in places the nudists' action inside the word for yearning

parts.note: to pine is to long or yearn
nudists strip off their clothes

explanation.surface: Nudists caught in long formal office suits, an absurd contrast.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit with thin vertical stripes is the classic City banker's outfit.

clue.text: Blows up leaves

explanation.surface: A short phrase that could be a storm scattering foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' reads like foliage but it is the verb to depart.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to explode, like a bomb, and to depart.

clue.text: Foreign double-agent the French let go, cutting down

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange and altered, so the letters are rearranged
let go tells us the French article is released from the mix

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A spy story: a foreign double agent the French release while cutting him down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' rearranges the letters of 'double-agent' once the French article LE is taken out by 'let go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Living within a tight budget means economising, reducing spending.

clue.text: No way drink is an answer to all problems

parts.note: taken as written
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A sober claim that drink is no way to solve life's problems.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack remedy claimed to cure everything is a panacea, a supposed universal solution.

clue.text: Letter delivery with Mike not well represented

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ailing means sick, not well

explanation.surface: Letters being delivered while Mike, the postman, is unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: The act of sending out post is the sending of letters by post.

clue.text: Initial report, you might say, quite literally!

definitions.text: Initial report, you might say, quite literally!

parts.words: Initial report, you might say, quite literally!
parts.note: the explosion said to begin the universe was the very first report, a loud noise

explanation.surface: A journalist's first dispatch on something, described as literally as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' looks like a news story but is a loud bang, the sound of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmic explosion that started the universe was the first loud noise of all time.

clue.text: One of the herd in New York city

definitions.meaning: a bison is one animal in a grazing herd
a city in upstate New York near Niagara Falls

explanation.surface: A conformist in the big city.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a herd animal, the American bison, and also a city on Lake Erie in New York State.

clue.text: Instant sign of approval

definitions.meaning: a moment, as in just a second
a check mark showing something is correct

explanation.surface: A quick nod of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal for a moment and also the check mark that shows something is right.

clue.text: Hidden treasure, sounds like 23, perhaps

indicators.note: sounds like tells us to take a word that is pronounced the same

parts.note: 23 down is EUROS, an example of cash

explanation.surface: Buried loot that may be euros.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard stored away in secret is a stash, hidden valuables.

clue.text: It's more fun arranging an accident!

indicators.note: arranging means putting the letters of the phrase into a new order

explanation.surface: A prankster says staging a mishap is more fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranging' reshuffles the letters of 'It's more fun'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap or piece of bad luck is an unfortunate event.

clue.text: Thus regret returning the money

indicators.note: returning tells us both pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: so means thus or therefore
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Someone regrets giving back their cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of the eurozone is a form of money in Europe.

clue.text: Old French master turned up briefly

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, backwards
briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: Edgar Degas was a French painter, an old master

explanation.surface: An elderly French master painter shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the last letter of DEGAS to leave DEGA, which 'turned up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Being old means elderly, having lived many years.

clue.text: Unknown woman in love with acting, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests other arrangements of the letters are allowed

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A mystery woman who has fallen for the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: IN is taken as written, then 'possibly' rearranges O and ACTING into COGNITA.
explanation.definitionFit: The feminine form of the Latin-derived word for someone in disguise or anonymous.

clue.text: Persuade a German to show willing

indicators.note: to show indicates the answer is on display within the run of words

explanation.surface: Trying to talk a German into proving he is game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Persuade' looks like a synonym clue, but the answer sits inside 'persuadE A GERman'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being keen to do something means being ready and wanting to act.

clue.text: Correct English leads to modest employment, no doubt

indicators.note: leads to points at the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Good English is the route to a humble job, surely.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend or revise a text is to correct its errors.

clue.text: In Polish it is an impediment to clear speech

parts.note: gloss is a shine or polish
taken as written

explanation.surface: In the Polish language it is an obstacle to clear speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the tongue makes talking difficult, so it hampers speech.
